summary: Transitive proxy duplicates subject claim when forwarding SSO -> service account role mapping fails
description:
Issue summary: Customer observed sudden 401/403 on calls that previously worked after a network edge change. Impact: Customer's admin service account could not perform tenant-scoped actions; production workflows blocked for a subset of service APIs. Root cause suspected in auth header transformation by a transitive proxy in the customer's edge stack.

High-level symptoms:
- Admin API calls from ClarityHealth's platform returned 403 with 'role-binding-not-found' in our authz logs.
- Identity and access logs showed 'sub' claim values that contain duplicated tenant prefixes (e.g., 'tenant:tenant:service-account@example.com').

This ticket captures investigation, proofs, and the remediation applied.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer infra: request flows through an external transitive proxy (tenant edge) before hitting Redwood Private ingress
Proxy configured to add tenant prefix to incoming 'sub' or X-Principal headers for multi-tenant routing
Send an authenticated request using a service account token with subject 'service-account@example.com'
Observe forwarded header contains 'tenant:tenant:service-account@example.com' (duplicated tenant prefix) and Redwood RBAC fails to match the expected subject canonical form
Reproduceable in staging by enabling the customer's proxy plugin that performs subject prefixing
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: token introspection and RBAC canonicalization mismatch after proxy transformation

Confirmed with customer: recent upgrade to their transitive proxy (v2.7.1) introduced an optional tenant-prefix plugin; default behavior was to prefix existing subject rather than idempotently ensure single prefix
Reproduced in Redwood staging by deploying same proxy plugin and enabling prefixing: observed identical duplicated-subject header and RBAC lookup failure
Auth service attempted to normalize 'sub' by stripping known prefixes, but logic only removed a single prefix, so 'tenant:tenant:service-account@...' remained unmatched
No evidence of token corruption; ID token signatures validated successfully and introspection passed — failure is in subject canonicalization for role binding lookup

resolution: Hotpatch deployed: added idempotent tenant-prefix canonicalizer in the auth service to collapse repeated tenant prefixes prior to RBAC lookup; also recommended customer disable redundant prefixing in their proxy config. Patch merged and rolled to prod us-east canary then full cluster. Follow-ups: add e2e test for proxy subject permutations and update troubleshooting runbook.
